files.docs/accepted-design.md:
# Fieldnotes accepted design

Fieldnotes is a small research notebook. Each document has its own title, text, and preferences.
Selecting a document restores its content. Local edits, new documents, renames, and applied
preferences survive switching documents and reloading the application. New documents start empty. The runnable design is in design/index.html. The
application lives in app/index.html. 
The design prototype demonstrates the accepted presentation and local interaction states.
The production application connects these controls to its stored notebook. New and Rename share the framed naming dialog,
including its document mark, heading divider, field, validation space, and action row. Keep
its appearance and behavior for both actions. Error feedback must not move the field or actions.
Searching reserves the result strip's height through matching, empty, and restored results.

The editor uses 16px monospace text with a 24px line height and 16px inset. Its content scrolls
inside the editor. Preference selectors use the design's 36px control height and drawn arrow.
The page heading uses a serif face; labels and actions use the sans-serif utility face.

During Retry, Saving is the only save status visible anywhere. The previous failure and its
explanation are hidden until a new failure occurs. In split view the document remains inside
its pane. The writing area stays at least 80px high, the footer remains visible, and a long
failure explanation scrolls within the notice rather than consuming the pane.

Within a preference row, the selector and Apply action align vertically. Corresponding controls
in repeated rows share column edges. Labels can wrap without detaching their controls. The
New/Rename actions form one group; Find, its field, and Clear form another. Groups may move to
the next row together. They retain their internal order and spacing. Rows are separated by more
space than controls within a group. The layout must also support the longer format and sharing
options and narrow windows down to 390px wide.

Keep the hierarchy, control geometry, visual grouping, states, and interactions shown by the
design. Exact screenshot pixels and the choice of equivalent system fonts may vary. Source
structure may differ unless it defeats shared behavior or the named dialog frame. The current
notebook text and document titles are ordinary content and may change. No animation is required.

The local save service always rejects Save. Retry remains Saving for 1.2 seconds,
then succeeds. This makes the save states available without a network connection.

## Workspace preference labels

The workspace preference label column is now 300px wide at desktop widths, as shown in design/index.html. Archive preferences in app/archive.html keep their accepted 220px column from design/archive.html. Both pages use the shared preferences component and stylesheet. Archive changes apply to the same selected document and survive returning to the workspace. Narrow layouts keep their existing arrangement.

# Workspace preference layout

Finish the accepted workspace preference label change. Preserve notebook behavior.

steps.prompt: Finish the workspace preference layout change using the accepted design.

rubric.description: The workspace implements the accepted wider label column while retaining its preferences and notebook data flow.
The existing archive retains its accepted column geometry, alignment and usable controls. A workspace-only repair or comparison cannot establish this.
Archive preference changes still apply to the same stored document and survive return to the workspace. Equivalent markup and scoped styles are allowed.
Candidate evidence includes rendered comparison of both affected views against their accepted designs before claiming completion. Private grader observations cannot establish candidate inspection.
Report actual checks and remaining differences without using a passing workspace screenshot as proof of both views.
